scope: Independent source-to-final-render exterior review of the 2018 NTUH Bam-Wood Hut. Not dimensional/as-built certification or independent execution of mesh QA.
source_viewing: All 15 original photographs/presentation sheets personally viewed during research; architect01/03/05/07/08/09/10 reopened during final review. Final front viewed after bamboo revision, remaining four final images individually viewed after completion; all five match current render-manifest SHA256.
confirmed: Distinct NTUH International Convention Center forecourt pavilion, not conference/hospital building itself; 2018 photographed appearance only.
20 timber transverse frames / 19 bays and two 20-post rows; original photo count independently cross-checked, not inferred from length.
Rows and eaves narrow toward longitudinal centre; ridge lowers centrally and rises at both ends. Cross-sectional roof slopes unequal, no equal-gable substitute.

Six-segment inner bamboo tension polygons now have near-horizontal upper chain, separated below timber rafters by elongated grey steel supports; revision avoids the earlier overly pointed inner gable.
Both ends and long sides open; longitudinal tunnel, between-frame gaps and bamboo/rafter airspaces remain open.
Rectangular raised deck with small access step, roof physically continuous with translucent presentation; no neighboring sculpture/tree/building merged.
Side diagonal ties are not indiscriminate per-bay double-X infill. Top/rear/oblique show complete roof and rear architecture.
explicit_estimates_and_limits: Per-bay single diagonal connection sequence and reversal at centre are simplified photo-guided estimates, not independently resolved every-joint as-built mapping.
Curve coefficients, frame station coordinates, ridge offset, bamboo nodes, panel/board joints and small steel hardware remain approximate; no structural engineering or measured-scale claim.
Design specification H5.2m vs section4.2–5.0m vs magazine5m not silently resolved as surveyed.
Fine members strengthened, platform hidden core simplified; support requirements and erosion/thin-part warnings remain meaningful.
STL cannot encode optical translucency; colour/Blend material effects do not imply transparent printed plastic.
Photo EXIF2018 capture and later editing dates distinguished; no 2026 condition claim. Original source photos remain private, links/metadata only in public package.
